doc.title: Anne Phillips interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 24, 2025

title: Bending Towards the Light: history, PBS attempt and publishing
summary: The holiday show has run nearly forty years; a PBS broadcast fell through and publishers want TV exposure.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: I totally agree. So briefly “Bending Towards the Light” is in — how many years now?
This will be the 40th if I do it this year.
If you do it this year.

It’s been done — last year it was the first time in Tucson, it’s been done for 30 years in Greensboro, North Carolina, they do it every single year. And Bozeman, Montana they did it. But the problem is that unless you can prove to a publisher — I was with Schirmer for the first ten years, and the only performances that came through Schirmer were ones that I found. And then I took it back, and now I have shipped it myself. But unless you can get it on television — and we did have a wonderful producer who is a major producer who did it for PBS and she presented it to them. And we had everybody — Dave Brubeck, Lionel Hampton, Tito Puente, you name it. And the place to do it — we were going to do it in October at the Apollo so it could be on the air, and they said yes to it. However you’ll have to bring it to us ready for air. You know what that means?
It means a lot of money.

It means a hell of a lot of money. At that point it was $350,000 was the budget. And that’s nowhere near what it would be today. And so the publishers, now Samuel French did publish a childrens’ show, The Great Gray Ghost of Old Spook Lane. Anyway I went to talk to them recently and I couldn’t find them, because they have now been bought by Concord Theatricals. Concord Theatricals is another big — it was Concord Records the jazz label originally, of California. But it has grown and it now owns Andrew Lloyd Weber, Bernstein — or whatchacalit — Hammerstein — Rogers & Hammerstein, all of that they license. And so to license it they want to know that it’s going to sell like crazy the first year. Well if it’s not on television then nobody knows what it is. So that’s where I am after all this time, because it’s been done in about 40, 50 cities. And every place it’s been done by their local people.
Well in New York it’s done —
